title: Interference: do two families pull the weights in opposite directions, and where
design_ref: Interference: detect it, then reduce it
purpose: Take the gradient of each family's RL loss on a probe batch, on the untrained model and on the model trained on the equal mixture, and compare the families' gradients module by module. The whole-model cosine is one number; the design says to look per module.

checks.description: the probe ran on both models for all six families, with a non-zero gradient for each
checks.because: A family whose probe prompts all scored the same has no advantage and no gradient; 32 prompts per family with four answers each were enough for every family here.

checks.description: the whole-model cosines are small (at most 0.15 in absolute value for every pair, on both models)
checks.because: Two gradients of 0.6 billion numbers each, dominated by many modules that do not interact, come out nearly orthogonal when summed over the whole model: the design's first warning.

notes: Two predictions written down before the probe ran, and what it said. (1) Per module the picture differs from the whole-model cosine: for at least one pair ten or more large modules with a cosine below -0.2: FAILED (the most for any pair on either model was 7; the lowest module cosine was -0.23). (2) The negative share of a pair is reproducible between the untrained and the trained model (Spearman above 0.3): FAILED (-0.16). The reading I draw: with 32 prompts per family, six families whose gradients are mostly noise at this scale, and a model this small, the probe does not separate pairs; what it does show is that no module is strongly conflicted, so the interference of the matrix (S03) is not a property of a few modules that a gradient probe can name here. A probe that is not reproducible between two nearby models is not an instrument yet; the design's own advice, to measure the noise first, applies to it as much as to the matrix.

Spearman correlation across the 15 pairs between the probe's negative share and the matrix's mean transfer of the pair: +0.21 (a negative value means more conflict where there is less transfer). I did not set a threshold on this correlation in advance: the claim is only that the two instruments, an evaluation delta and a gradient probe, can be compared on the same pairs.
